After breakfast, a transfer to the airport is provided for your flight home.

Over the week, the route changes its setting completely several times. At the start of the trip, you walk along the ocean and see Rio from Sugar Loaf, then spend a night at the Sambadrome, climb through the Tijuca Forest to Christ the Redeemer and fly on to the tropical waterfalls.

Carnival and Iguazu leave very different impressions. One brings music, lights, costumes, thousands of people and a city at night. The other brings water, forest, cool spray and the constant roar of the cascades. Together, they offer an eventful introduction to Brazil in 8 days.

You will remember not only the main sights but also the journeys between them: the warm breeze at Copacabana, the view of the city from Urca, the train through Tijuca, a night amid the drums, the humid air of Iguazu and the boardwalks that take you almost within touching distance of the roaring water.

blocks.text:
In Rio, city life revolves around the ocean, music and preparations for Carnival. In Iguazu, water shapes the experience: first comes a low rumble beyond the trees, then the cascades, mist and broad gorge appear. This combination makes for an especially varied route: in one trip, you experience a grand city celebration, tropical forest and one of South America's most impressive waterfall systems.

**Group departure:** 05.02 - 12.02

## Travel highlights

In Rio, you will take the cable car up Sugar Loaf. The first stop is on Urca Hill, before the cabin climbs higher to the main viewpoint. From here, you can see Copacabana, Guanabara Bay, islands, the Niterói Bridge and the green mountains around the city.

After the panoramas, the route returns to the streets. The old centre preserves churches, monasteries, the main cathedral and colonial facades. Here, Rio's variety is especially clear: in the morning you face the ocean and mountains; a few hours later, you are among narrow streets, historic buildings and a bustling centre.

Another high viewpoint is on Corcovado. The little train passes through the Tijuca Forest, past damp tree trunks, vines and vivid tropical greenery. The statue of Christ the Redeemer stands at the summit. From the viewing area, you can see Sugar Loaf, Guanabara Bay, the Botanical Garden, Maracanã and neighbourhoods stretching between the water and the mountains.

The main night in Rio takes place at the Sambadrome. Samba schools appear one after another, each with its own theme, costumes, music and huge floats. Drum sections set the pace along the entire avenue, the stands join in the songs and the parade continues late into the night.

In Iguazu, you first see the falls from the Brazilian side. A sweeping panorama opens up: the river splits into many streams, water plunges from basalt ledges and mist constantly hangs over the gorge. There are around 275 cascades in the area.

The next day, the route explores the Argentine side. Paths and boardwalks run above the broad river, descend towards the lower cascades and rise again to the viewpoints. The water is close, spray reaches your face and, at Devil's Throat, the noise grows so loud that conversation is almost lost in the roar.

Another advantage of the route is the free time between excursion days. In Rio, spend it at Copacabana, Ipanema or Leblon, sit in a café by the ocean and watch the city prepare for Carnival. In Iguazu, there is time to rest after the journey before 2 long walks through the national parks.

The programme connects arrivals, transfers and excursions in one route. Carnival tickets and the hotel - Sambadrome - hotel transfer are included. The domestic flight between Rio and Iguazu is paid separately, while the sequence of the trip is already arranged to move from 4 nights in Rio to 3 nights by the falls.
